title: CI runs at milestones, not on every merge, and you get options on best practice
why: Your gripe, Oct 27 (waiting page, item 27): "Not only drop the exception, I merge so arbitrarily and can merge so often that frankly I still find the amount of CI used to be preposterous. I think there may be something in this roadmap already of essentially wanting \"milestone-style\" reviews of CI -- I think my Q_Max repo might have some examples of that where I got so sick of my CI bill that I was like look orchestrator after u see a ton has landed then yes run a check but not every merge. That could be me not doing best practices, and I'm eager to learn, and/but I want some help here"
note: No earlier step covers it (checked roadmap d0c17e61; c39, CI time caps, is done and about caps, not volume). Item 27 (c69) answered a: drop the per-lane full CI job exception; the build advisor (6) has it. Part 1 done Oct 27 (doc: https://claude.ai/artifact/XMDQP1nVCuq3u35qvwE8eV, sent to the waiting page). Measured Oct 13-27 at main 2ad85de: about 16,800 runner-minutes a week; the run after each merge to main is 38% of it and ended green 4 of 48 times last week, mostly cut off at Windows and Chromium time caps. Pick C: one scoped run per batch, batches cut at about 4 waiting lanes or 3 hours, no run on main and no nightly, a full run at milestones the build advisor names; estimate about 2,400 a week. Needs first: a trustworthy full run, and a batch proved against current main (strict is false today). Part 2, deferred (shiv, Oct 27): you choose; the rule lands in the global CLAUDE.md (rule roles-each-layer-proves-once, git-integration-branch-merge) and the gates workflows. Port: yes; the rule is global, each repo's workflows follow at its visit. Placed ahead of c82, after c88 (triage, Oct 27): CI spend grows with every merge. Deferred (shiv, Oct 27): part 2's picks are yours. Asked: waiting page item c95-ci-milestones.
